title: Manufacturing processes
examples: What is the difference between casting and moulding?
Can you show me an example of a joining technique?
How does the scale of production affect the design?

explain.say: Today we will explore how things are made in factories.
Casting is when you pour a liquid material into a space.
Moulding involves shaping a material, often using a mould cavity.
Joining techniques connect two or more separate pieces together.
The scale of production means how many items are made.
In everyday life, making a plastic toy shows these skills.

faq.q: What is the main difference between casting and moulding?
faq.a: Casting usually involves pouring a liquid metal into a mould. Moulding can involve shaping a softer material like plaster or clay within a mould.
asks: Is moulding always for soft things?
Do I pour things for casting?

faq.q: When would I use joining techniques?
faq.a: You use joining techniques when you need to connect two pieces of material permanently. This could be connecting wood or metal parts.
asks: How do I stick things together strongly?
What is the strongest way to join metal?

faq.q: What does 'scale of production' really mean?
faq.a: It refers to the volume of goods being made, from making just one unique item to making thousands quickly.
asks: What is the difference between small and large scale?

faq.q: Can you use these processes on wood?
faq.a: While casting is for liquids, moulding and joining can certainly be used with wood. You might mould plaster around a wooden object.

faq.q: Is there a difference between gluing and welding?
faq.a: Gluing uses an adhesive that chemically bonds surfaces together. Welding involves using intense heat to melt and fuse the materials at the joint.
asks: What is the process of welding?

facts: Casting requires a pattern that is often made of wax or plastic.
Moulds create a negative impression of the original object.
Welding is a strong method for joining metals.
Bespoke items are made at a very small scale of production.

quiz.say: A jewellery maker pours melted silver into a carved container to make a ring. What process is this?
quiz.why: Casting involves pouring a liquid material, like melted silver, into a mould.

wrong.0: Bespoke describes the scale, not the physical making process itself.
wrong.2: Moulding usually involves shaping a softer material, not pouring liquid metal.
wrong.3: Joining connects two separate pieces, but here the object is formed as one piece.

quiz.say: If you attach a metal bracket to a wooden shelf using a strong, permanent metal pin, what technique are you using?
quiz.why: Joining techniques are used specifically to connect two or more separate parts together.

wrong.0: Moulding shapes material around a form, it does not connect two existing pieces.
wrong.1: This describes the scale, not the physical action of connecting the parts.
wrong.3: Casting forms an object from liquid, it does not connect pre-made parts.

quiz.say: A factory produces one thousand identical plastic chairs using automated machinery. This represents what scale of production?
quiz.why: Making a very large, identical number of items is called mass production.

wrong.1: Bespoke means making only one unique item for one person.
wrong.2: Small batch means making a few items, not a thousand.
wrong.3: A prototype is an early model, not the final large output number.
